correctness.rationale: For each quantifier rank the truncation of block sizes to the rank preserves Ehrenfeucht–Fraïssé equivalence; the finite coloured-word type monoid is aperiodic by the repeated-block order game. The labelled total-preorder EGF is exactly a finite resolvent of an entire transition matrix. Its positive stochastic specialization has convergent powers and harmonic projection; the derivative on the peripheral eigenspace is twice the identity. All nonpositive-complex-circle points have strictly smaller absolute row sums because the aggregated large-block letter includes consecutive positive powers. A unique simple dominant pole therefore yields a full-sentence exponential convergence law and a computable limit in the field generated by log 2. Explicit Fubini and first/last-block exact identities were independently checked by exhaustive two-method enumeration through seven worlds; these finite checks are corroboration, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The theorem evaluates limiting probabilities of every fixed first-order sentence in a natural nontrivial random finite model class with a complete uniform-labelled sampling definition, effective finite linear-algebra calculation, and sentence-dependent exponential convergence. It separates a genuine non-zero-one convergence law from classical enumerative Fubini asymptotics. A two-ended boundary pattern has a further explicit nontrivial limit, illustrating more than a repeated census of the least block.
